what_this_is: Cincinnati's first Marriott scale batch under the policy Order 015 measured: one first attempt, then at most one same-lane retry for a row that came back with no usable page. Run as two explicit passes so the two-attempt ceiling is a property of the run, not a hope about the router.

authorization.why_fewer_than_authorised: 17 rows at two attempts and the settled $0.16 is a worst case of $5.44 -- exactly the cap -- which would have left the prepaid balance at $0.21. Phase 3 required reducing the cohort rather than doing that, so 14 rows were admitted, worst case $4.48, floor preserved at $1.17.
authorization.stratification: all 13 Marriott sub-brands in the 34-row pool are represented, and 9 of 11 cities. URL template and property-code shape could NOT be stratified: every pool row is /en-us/hotels/<code>-<slug>/overview with a 5-character code, so those axes have exactly one stratum each.

comparison.do_these_differ: NOT established. The Wilson intervals overlap ([0.137, 0.694] against [0.454, 0.883]). The honest reading is that first-attempt access is VARIABLE between runs, which is an argument FOR keeping the retry rather than evidence the wall has weakened.
comparison.pooled_caveat: this batch alone retried only TWO challenge rows, so its 0/2 has a Wilson upper bound of 0.66 and settles nothing by itself. Pooled with Order 015's five, the rate is 0 of 7 and the upper bound is still 0.35. Zero repeats seven times running is the best evidence available; it is not proof, and the next batch must measure it again.

marriott_recommendation.policy: first attempt plus at most one same-lane retry
marriott_recommendation.why: 0 of 2 retried challenge rows repeated, and the batch finished 14 of 14 publication grade
marriott_recommendation.what_would_retire_it: a repeat-challenge rate at or above 25% in any later batch. The rate must be measured again each time; a policy that stops checking the number it depends on is an assumption wearing a measurement's clothes.

evidence_binding.rule: approvals bind document_sha256, never block_sha256 alone
evidence_binding.why: Order 015 found two unrelated properties sharing the identical block 'Pet Policy Pets Not Allowed'. This batch reproduces the problem at larger scale: 14 rows yield only 10 distinct block digests, because several properties refuse in exactly the same words. All 14 DOCUMENT digests are distinct, so identity-specific binding is available for every row.

cost.note: the balance delta is the operative meter and is the smallest of the three; the ledger's reserved figure is a ceiling the runner enforces against, never a bill. Both are reported because using the reserved figure as actual spend would overstate cost by nearly 50%.

settled_rate.why_the_higher: the two meters disagree by roughly 60%. Planning on the cheaper one is how a batch discovers mid-run that it cannot finish.
